prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1483; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by phone this morning after a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. Insured driver is listed on the policy and reports that the claimant was the front-seat passenger in the other vehicle, which is consistent with the police report.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and recorded the claimant as present in the vehicle. Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the insured's account of how the impact occurred.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene show frontal damage to both vehicles that is consistent with the reported speed and angle of impact. The other driver's statement describes the collision the same way.

Entry 4: Claimant reported a head injury with headache and dizziness and was taken to hospital by ambulance. Diagnosis on attendance was concussion, which fits the nature of the impact.

Entry 5: Claimant's account at the hospital and in our first recorded call matches the scene evidence. Medical records show no prior treatment to the head or neck in the records available to us.

Entry 6: Claimant is now represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office. Received a letter requesting the full medical file and confirmed our handling of the claim.

Entry 7: Inspection of the claimant's vehicle found a dent in the panel at the point of impact. A dated photo from an earlier inspection shows the same dent, which conflicts with the reported timing of the damage and needs to be reviewed.

Entry 8: Checked the policy start date and the coverage history. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before coverage began, and the insured driver is named on the policy as a listed driver.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued for longer than is typical for a concussion of this kind, with follow-up appointments still being booked. Counsel has provided updated treatment notes, which we are reviewing against the earlier records.

Entry 10: Claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation so far. The file remains open pending the review of the earlier dented-panel photo and the ongoing medical records.
